subject: Business continuity questionnaire — RTO/RPO, multi-region failover (Redwood response)
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@globex.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.example.com>; Globex Procurement <procurement_globex@globex.com>
Date: 2025-11-03T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Globex BCDR questionnaire — Redwood

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week. As part of our procurement process we need Redwood to complete our business continuity and disaster recovery questionnaire (attached). The key items our security and infra teams want clarified are:
- RTO and RPO targets for hosted API and Dedicated deployments
- Multi-region failover behaviour for both active-active and active-passive modes
- Expected client-visible failover window (time-to-first-successful-response)
- How session state (chat history/KV cache) is preserved or recovered across a region failover
- Cadence of DR tests and evidence you can share

Please return the completed questionnaire and any supporting runbooks or test summaries by COB Friday so our risk team can review. If it helps, we can do a call to walk through answers.

Thanks,
Samantha
Senior Security Program Manager
Globex Corporation
Attachment: Globex_BCDR_Questionnaire_v3.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.example.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2025-11-03T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Globex BCDR questionnaire — can you draft responses?

Folks,

Forwarding Globex's questionnaire. Security will want the precise wording; ops needs to confirm test evidence we can share. High priority — they want this by COB Friday.

Initial thoughts (high level):
- RTO: For production-hosted API endpoints we aim for sub-60s failover for user-visible requests when configured with multi-region active-active routing. For Dedicated clusters with cross-region replication enabled we target <5 minutes for full recovery of persistent state depending on workload.
- RPO: For stateless inference the RPO is effectively zero (requests can be reissued). For session state (cached KV/session histories) we provide asynchronous replication by default in Hosted; RPO "near-zero" can be achieved with synchronous replication profiles for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Failover window: automatic routing failover is typically detected and rerouted within 20-90s depending on client DNS/circuit behavior; if clients use our SDK with health checks it is closer to 10-30s.
- DR tests: quarterly full failover drills; monthly tabletop; we can provide redacted runbooks and test summaries.

Mina, can you: 1) turn these into precise questionnaire answers, 2) confirm which artifacts from Q3 we can attach (runbook + redacted test logs), and 3) call out modes where behaviour differs (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).

Grace, ops could you validate the Dedicated numbers and the recommended replication profile names (sync/async) and any config knobs we should reference in the document.

Thanks — k

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.example.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.example.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2025-11-03T11:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Globex BCDR questionnaire — can you draft responses?

Karthik (and Grace),

I've drafted formal answers and pulled the SRE runbook excerpts that are safe to share. Key clarifications I added to the draft:

- Hosted API (default):
  - RTO (user-visible): 20-90 seconds for request reroute depending on client retry/backoff; average observed 35s in Q3 controlled drills (see attached test summary).
  - RPO (session state): Default async replication; best-effort for in-flight requests. We preserve committed session checkpoints (conversation save points) with typically <30s lag; in-flight uncommitted tokens may be lost and should be treated as transient. For customers requiring stronger guarantees we recommend the "Guaranteed Sync" replication profile available for Redwood Dedicated and Private.

- Dedicated:
  - RTO: with cross-region active-active configuration and Kafka-backed change-log replication we achieve automated failover with RTO < 5 minutes for full state convergence; user-visible reroute often <60s if application-level retries are configured.
  - RPO: can be configured to near-zero using synchronous replication; if configured async, typical RPO is <1 minute.

- Private (on-prem/VPC): behaviour depends on customer networking and DR architecture; we provide runbook guidance and an optional SRE-engaged DR run to validate assumptions.

- Multi-region architecture notes:
  - Active-active: global load balancer + per-region inference clusters + KV replication. Seamless for stateless calls; session continuity depends on replication profile.
  - Active-passive: faster state convergence but requires DNS/route change; expected client-visible failover 30s–5min depending on TTL settings and health-check cadence.

- DR test cadence & artifacts: quarterly full restoration drills (redacted logs attached), monthly health-checks, and continuous synthetic traffic monitoring. We can provide a redacted Q3 drill packet (includes timeline, failover detection, time-to-first-successful-response metrics).

Attachments I can include: BCDR_Annex_A_SRE_Runbook.pdf, Redwood_DR_Test_Results_Q3_2025.zip (redacted). I recommend we avoid publishing raw logs and instead share summarized metrics and runbook excerpts.

I will convert this to the questionnaire format and return a PDF for external submission.

— Mina
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

Samantha / Daniel,

Thanks for the questionnaire — attached is our completed response (PDF) and supporting artifacts summarized for Globex:

Highlights (excerpt):
- Hosted API: user-visible RTO (automatic client routing) typically 20–90s; average 35s in Q3 drill. RPO for session checkpoints typically <30s with default async replication; in-flight tokens not durably persisted.
- Dedicated: configurable synchronous replication gives near-zero RPO and full-state RTO <5 minutes for cross-region active-active clusters; async mode typical RPO <1 minute.
- Multi-region failover: active-active provides fastest user experience; active-passive depends on DNS/TTL and expected 30s–5min window.
- DR testing: Quarterly full failovers (we ran one in Q3 2025 — summary attached), monthly tabletop, continuous monitoring.

Attachments: Redwood_BCDR_Response_2025-11-03.pdf, BCDR_Annex_A_SRE_Runbook.pdf, Redwood_DR_Test_Results_Q3_2025.zip

If helpful, I'd be happy to set up a 30-minute call with our SRE and product lead to walk through the technical details and any specific scenarios your risk team wants validated. Please let me know a few times that work.

Best,
Karthik
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
